answer: An agent market weights a vote by the square of its account's locked bond, with no per-account subsidy. The bond ledger acts as a lantern through a karst of forwarding wallets: renaming funds creates no capital. Splitting B into n equal bonds yields total weight B squared/n, versus B squared in one account. At a fixed budget, one identity is the zenith of influence; buying more influence requires more locked capital. This discourages cloning, but favors wealthy incumbents and does not establish unique ownership.
